text: **Cobblestone pavement** is most common in the northeast and in Rio Grande do Sul.
The section of NR15 from Muhanga till the Western Province border has very **poor pavement**, with a lot of potholes and a lack of road lines.

The section of NR15 from the Western Province border to [this point](https://maps.app.goo.gl/g4dL5u31ULbJrdXw9) is under construction, with no pavement at the moment; making it the only covered National Road to be unpaved for this long. Also, most of the road hugs a steep cliffside made of red dirt.
NOTE: Non-national roads are often unpaved, but they are usually not as wide, and have more stuff going on around them.
Many roads in **Butare** feature **cobblestone pavement**.

Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have **rumble strips** on each edge of the road, which are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road. These can be located on the outside edges of the road and in between lanes on multi-lane highways.
NOTE: Rumble strips may appear in Canada, but are much more rare.
These **rectangular raised pavement markers** are found in the south and west of the US and also in Massachusetts.
**Snowplowable raised pavement markers** can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

Rectangular pavement markers **each on the side of the double lines** are commonly found in Georgia, Florida, Texas, and California. Other rectangular RPM states have the RPM between the double lines.
NOTE: Beware of similar patterns in left turn lanes.
Roads with **reddish pavement **lined with **long **[**Argentine needle-grass**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nassella_tenuissima)** **are common in San Luis.
The pavement which the trekker walks on in Minsk is mostly **grey rectangular tiles**. On a small part, there are [pink-ish tiles](https://goo.gl/maps/jBJvXJYu2yqYENLw9) in a specific pattern.
This type of pavement, consisting of rectangular **grey bricks **with slightly wavy edges, is very common in El Alto.
The section of Ruta 5 around Chaco, just north of Sucre, has distinct **sunset coverage**. Most of this road has concrete pavement, and meanders through semi-arid hills.
The section of Ruta 6 between Tarabuco and Zudáñez is paved with **extremely light-coloured concrete**, bordering on white. This pavement is very recognizable and unique to this road.

Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and **tar snakes** are frequently seen. In the east, many [**dead trees**](https://goo.gl/maps/vvvheTYM3U7XohwK9) can be seen with a lack of leaves.
Bantam Village can be recognized by the **cross-hatched** brick pavement.
In Colombia, it is particularly common for sidewalks to be decorated with **reddish tiles**.
Another major divided highway is the RN 32 from the intersection with RN 4 to Limón on the Caribbean coast. The road passes through lush forests in the generally flat Northern lowlands.
NOTE: Aside from the stretch of the RN 1 with concrete pavement, all other major divided highways are in close proximity to San José.

The Punta Leona Resort, which can be found by the “Playa Mantas” POI, can be recognised by the **red brick pavement**, with the bricks having the same shape as you’ll commonly find in [Turkey](https://www.google.com/maps/@40.7468922,31.6196471,3a,48.1y,163.7h,64.62t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sxgSFnYGwZ7tHRph3WXoxAA!2e0!7i16384!8i8192?entry=ttu).
Most of the coverage in Filadelfia de Guanacaste was taken on the edge of a park, with a distinct red brick pavement where the bricks are placed in the shape of an “L”.

Croatia’s capital Zagreb has a distinct **big city feel**. Apartment** **blocks can be seen throughout the city. The northern part of the city is hilly. Furthermore, Zagreb has [blue electric trams](https://goo.gl/maps/HKezsyENV7j4TJ1J7).
NOTE: In addition to regular car coverage, Zagreb also has various urban [sidewalk trekkers](https://goo.gl/maps/55CGuPvKbjzGLv4XA), often made with a Generation 2 camera.

Streets in downtown Prague are commonly paved with grey and white marble stones, which is also typical for Portugal. They’re often arranged in intricate square mosaics, but some sections are far more [plain](https://maps.app.goo.gl/oUoxqu29WmRibzCF7). NOTE: Similar pavement can be found in much lower volume in [other towns](https://maps.app.goo.gl/yiUMPdyLTC8wHtAB8) too. Consider the apparent size of the city before guessing Prague.
In urban areas, you can sometimes find this pavement consisting of **hexagonal tiles**.

Åland roads have two unique aspects that separate them from the rest of Finland: their pavement tends to have a **red tint**, and they have **dashed** outside road lines that resemble those found in Sweden.
Downtown Helsinki has a lot of Generation 4 **sidewalk trekker** coverage.
NOTE: This tip is specifically about Generation 4 trekker coverage. Generation 3 sidewalk trekkers can be found in many other Finnish cities.
The CA9, going between Escuintla and the coast, can be recognised by being a **divided highway** with **concrete pavement**.

**Raised pavement markers** in Hawaii will commonly be placed in a specific pattern: a single reflector, followed by four reflectors put close together and then a single reflector, repeating the pattern.
Distinct **bright orange** bins can be found on sidewalks.
Lung Wo Road can be recognized by the Hong Kong Island** skyline to the south** and the Kowloon skyline to the north. The road is also in good condition and the sidewalks are clean.

Lam Kam Road is similar to Fan Kam Road, however it runs in a more **east-west** direction. The road should also feel **busier **with more cars driving along the road and more houses on the sides of the road. In addition, the road is usually wider and a [median](https://goo.gl/maps/Yggjz9dCZCderyto9) containing trees can be seen separating sidewalks near the villages.
Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct **yellow outer road lines** and fresh dark pavement.
NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these [lines](https://goo.gl/maps/WVhAoJzbH15AGQoG6) exist in other states as well.
Snow prevention roads, known as ‘Shosetsu’, are found mainly in northwest coastal prefectures. They appear as **tiny circles **in the pavement, and spray warm underground water to clear snow.
The **A26 **goes from Kandyagash to the intersection of M32/E38.

It has very **bad road quality** throughout, ranging from [poor grainy pavement](https://goo.gl/maps/SutyRPAen8GPgGXP7), to [completely unpaved](https://goo.gl/maps/vAPBAKKBSqP1cY4y5). Apart from the northernmost section, the weather is either cloudy or overcast.
The landscape consists mostly of flat, semi-arid grassy plains.
Driving direction: **North **towards Kandyagash. (Mostly)

The **A17 **going to Ulytau Region can be recognised by the **bad pavement quality**, where the edges of the road are almost crumbling away, along with the **single white middle road line**, which can be dashed or solid. The landscape itself is a grassy steppe, with some fall coloured trees occasionally lining the roads.
[West of Atasu](https://goo.gl/maps/TdENdhe3WB985Lhi8), the sun is distinctly low on the horizon.
NOTE: A small section east of Atasu has [pristine new pavement](https://goo.gl/maps/XeJe82NWDfF4gH1K9), which has a slight red tint to it.
Driving direction: **Towards **[**Atasu**](https://www.google.com/maps/@48.6874387,71.6576538,13.19z?entry=ttu) from both directions

Going further south, you will reach this next valley, which seems equally dry, but the mountains are more rocky and have **trees** growing on them. The road now has very **bad pavement**, and as such you can see dust clouds.

This road going west of Naryn is situated south in the **dry** Naryn valley. You will typically see hills **close** to the road on the southern side. There are also bigger mountains not too far behind. While to the north, there is a wide plain, with hills and mountains in the distance. Many parts of the road also have a pavement with a [salt and pepper-like quality](https://www.google.com/maps/@41.4307504,75.7604242,3a,19.2y,69.61h,72.46t,0.49r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sfkTujXcKAOpKC3EtfhN0tg!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu).
Coverage was taken along parts of the promenade in Beirut, with a grey brick pavement and a large number of fan palms.
The ER211 can be recognized by the dark pavement combined with its exposed brownish soil.
**Grainy **pavement with a** blue-ish grey tinge** is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.
NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature [dashed outer lines](https://goo.gl/maps/J82S2uF1oZ7qGhEG6).

This style of **cobblestone pavement**, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
This pavement consisting of **hexagonal tiles** is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
This exact pavement design with **three lines** of cobblestone patterning is mainly found in Oaxaca.

The capital city, Ulaanbaatar, is by far the biggest city in Mongolia, with about 50% of the entire country's population living in it. As such, its urban development and sheer size is unlike anywhere else in Mongolia. The cityscape is bustling with many **high rise buildings**, chain stores, travelling cars, buses, and pedestrians, as well as clean roads and sidewalks. Meanwhile, the suburbs can be recognized from the [vast yurt districts](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.9272927,107.008841,3a,29.5y,301.6h,86.46t/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1sYXiArLUQKXIXelnn6G9MXQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) in **hilly areas**. Generation 4 coverage is common, however Generation 3 [winter coverage](https://www.google.com/maps/@47.809762,107.161727,3a,133.2y,242.8h,87.43t/data=!3m4!1e1!3m2!1sR3u-gHu194XNWIm0UrWpZw!2e0) is also common to see in the suburbs.

The other main desert highway in Mongolia runs through Mandalgovi, and can be differentiated from the Choir Highway by its **cloudy skies**, darker pavement, and deep blue tent instead of the tentless car.
This map shows pavement type as well as the driving direction on all major roads.
Between Gibeon and Tses, the road has wider shoulders, and the pavement quality in general is excellent.
You can recognise this long stretch of B8 by the **light coloured grainy pavement** as well as the general E-NE angle and vegetated northern landscape.

Red tinted and slightly grainy pavement along with the green savannah-like grassy landscape crowned with [low-lying cumulus clouds](https://maps.app.goo.gl/sThNdCyePnA6XouS9) can be used to recognise the northern section of road C35.

South of the C41 intersection, the road loses its red pavement, and the quality worsens. The landscape is less grassy, and more sandy, with [hills](https://maps.app.goo.gl/HByXtaekqiaUQGk77) to the west, though often hidden behind the vegetation. The road generally goes in a S-SE direction. Further south, it gets hillier, and parts will have a more SE bound angle. The sky is consistently covered by scattered [cirrostratus](https://maps.app.goo.gl/K6hbEGCHVQJKwN58A) and [cumulus](https://maps.app.goo.gl/d26SpmrumkcZVnv36) clouds.

East of the intersection with the C35, the road has a constant SW to NW angle, and grainy pavement. The grass looks soft to the touch, and the somewhat sandy soil is typical of this region. Cumulus clouds dot the sky.
[West of the C35 intersection](https://maps.app.goo.gl/9jXSgyXW1W6ZBLUL7), the same grainy pavement and clouds remain, but the landscape is much hillier, and the road angle changes.

Often fairly **poor quality pavement** with [only white road lines](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Jf6P3gTK1pfE144b9), [no road lines at all](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RNMAWUQFhJFheYrK6), or just slightly [faded road lines and red tinted pavement](https://maps.app.goo.gl/JyFSRjp81cNB64Wz6), are all good clues for the C49 in the panhandle. Near the western end, the [sun](https://maps.app.goo.gl/tGh9NAzuqvDdPpjF7) is very low in the sky, and the weather is fully clear.
NOTE: A [small section](https://maps.app.goo.gl/vvEApEqhL8fBQX6G6) by Makolonga has good pavement with wide shoulders, so look for the orange patches on the road.

The D3600 and the [unlabelled road](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RTqENPBLvJo7fsBd6) going NE to Mpungu, have a very light coloured, sometimes grainy pavement, with at times [very faded yellow lines](https://maps.app.goo.gl/X3ZNNmiVtCtcwsiC9), which are hard to even see. Combined with the either exactly N to S or NE angle, as well as the northern landscape, make this road very distinct.
A few roads in the north lack the typical outer yellows.

- The [C46](https://maps.app.goo.gl/A2iuCsBL27yXdx5L8), which is a long road going generally NW to SE. The [E-W section by Ruacana](https://maps.app.goo.gl/TkmT5fLgDYyqJGRC7), has very poor pavement. [SE of Oshikuku](https://maps.app.goo.gl/8ETt6hv4choo1q9B6), the sun is low in the sky to the NW.
- [C41 (M123)](https://maps.app.goo.gl/oe2n4NQt2GrYct8G6) also has a NW angle but has more clouds in the sky than the C46.
- [B10](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pj18CXj2apN1rFNF9) west of Eenhana is an E-W stretch, which is more vegetated, and also has the sun low in the sky to the west.

- [B10](https://maps.app.goo.gl/t2rL31dKFVdiAHhs7) east of Nkurenkuru is another NW bound stretch with the sun low in the sky, but this part is much more vegetated than the C46. You can also see the [moon](https://maps.app.goo.gl/DSwUn3Fn5S9pfiVW7) to the east.
- [D3615](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Xk6TXPZPYkXYuShh7) is a short road with a constant N-NE angle that technically has outer yellows, but they are quite faded.
Langstrand is a small resort town between Swakopmund and Walvis Bay with **pink brick sidewalks** next to essentially every road. The weather is always **overcast **and gloomy.
Most Dutch **sidewalks** use the same type of square grey tiles and offset tiling pattern. In some historic areas, you might find smaller [brick sidewalks](https://goo.gl/maps/57mi9meFyFNVCbun9).

**Baarle** is a town in the south of the Netherlands which contains a number of Belgian enclaves. Throughout the town, you can sometimes see signs of this, such as markings on the pavement and [Dutch and Belgian flags](https://goo.gl/maps/sKCBPk8vqM9AUrmB9) being flown together.

Just west of ميتان, only labelled in Arabic on Google Maps, literally translating to methane, there is a stretch of road, which has a uniquely light-coloured pavement. To the north, you can see [sand dunes](https://maps.app.goo.gl/EHoRRV2ud19p4Jbz9).

Neatly **tiled sidewalks** are very common in Poland. Tiles are often grey or light red. Occasionally, even roads have tiled pavement. Many different types of tile patterns occur, including [larger square tiles](https://goo.gl/maps/8S5B5uDchRQ47vD36).
Similarly, cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly **bright stones** are very common.

**Cobblestone pavement** is notably common in [Kaliningrad](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cAtPVWR2WxLiyS8V8), [Nizhny Tagil](https://maps.app.goo.gl/iUD3LBhJYxSxdHFeA) in Sverdlovsk, and [Kizel](https://goo.gl/maps/2rLUZD6Rvei7qWwXA) in Perm Krai.

Saint-Pierre is the capital and largest town. The coverage in this town is made with a **sidewalk trekker**. Larger buildings and more cars can be seen, with a more populated feel compared to Miquelon-Langlade.
You can find this **grainy**, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of **pink **in Limpopo.
The stretch of the E45 going between Orsa and Älvros can be recognised by the **brown-red wet pavement** with forest consisting of thin pines and birches along the roadside.
Pavement with **white speckles** is commonly found along the east coast.
text_zh: 帶有**白色斑點**的路面在東海岸相當常見。

text: The islands east of Taitung, Green Island and Orchid Island, are distinct due to the more **tropical** climate, abundance of coconut palms, and lush cliffs. Additionally, it is common to find run-down, **concrete** pavement.

NOTE: While the landscape between Green Island and Orchid Island are quite similar, a good way to distinguish the two is that Green Island frequently uses **yellow outer lines**. Additionally, Green Island is slightly more built-up.
text_zh: 台東東方的綠島與蘭嶼特徵鮮明：氣候更**熱帶**、椰子樹繁多、崖壁植被茂密，另外也常見老舊的**水泥**路面。
註：綠島與蘭嶼的地貌相當接近，但綠島經常使用**黃色邊線**，這是很好的分辨依據；此外綠島的開發程度也略高一些。

text: Lienchiang County, also referred to as the Matsu Islands, is recognizable from the hilly landscape and frequent use of **concrete roads**. The coverage is **overcast** and [this pavement](https://www.google.com/maps/@26.2025968,119.9695409,3a,48.8y,276.8h,91.84t,2.84r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s3KR53okaioyHthx43kE3bQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu) can also commonly be found.
text_zh: 連江縣（馬祖列島）可由丘陵地形與大量的**水泥路面**辨認。街景多為**陰天**拍攝，[這種路面](https://www.google.com/maps/@26.2025968,119.9695409,3a,48.8y,276.8h,91.84t,2.84r/data=!3m6!1e1!3m4!1s3KR53okaioyHthx43kE3bQ!2e0!7i13312!8i6656?entry=ttu)也很常見。

text: An offroad from road P12 southwest of Sousse can be recognised by the dark pavement surrounded by bright sandy soil combined with the east-west road angle. The eastern part of the road is fairly vegetated, with large numbers of prickly pears, while the western part of the road is [very arid](https://maps.app.goo.gl/W7Q3a5DgLqsJuio59) with little to no vegetation.
Many roads have pavement with a grainy “**salt and pepper**” texture.
**Brick pavement** is very common in urban areas, and the bricks will typically have the shape shown in the image.
A **poorly paved runway** can be seen going north to south on the Midway Atoll. The pavement gets increasingly poor to the [north](https://goo.gl/maps/d45BgC8WQFuxeAE67).

The **only paved road** with coverage outside Kampala can be found here. The pavement almost entirely lacks the red tinge which is typical for most roads in the country. The road has white, solid outer lines and a yellow middle line.
A power line runs parallel to the road, to your east. To your north, you will be able to see hills.
On average, Ukraine has some of the **worst roads** in Europe. Most rural roads have lots of potholes, cracks and warped pavement.
This abysmal road quality can really help with tough 50-50s with Russia, which generally has somewhat better roads.
Houses in residential areas are typically made of **light-coloured stone**. Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.
In some parts of Dubai, including the [old town](https://goo.gl/maps/CXsP5xq4fAtX7Ds47), a Generation 4 **sidewalk trekker** was used. Sometimes, the employee’s black hair is visible.
**Texan roads** often have a grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface.
NOTE: [Similar pavement](https://goo.gl/maps/ChBAJda4PYN38dJ1A) can sometimes be seen in adjacent states such as New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Colorado.

Some rural roads in the Upper Midwest use a similar road pavement to [Texas](https://goo.gl/maps/GeXiD3RdkjUkGMWr9). They will have a **grainy, ‘salt and pepper’-like road surface**, but will vary in colour. These roads are most common in the state of Illinois.
